questions.stem: A database contains 50 relevant documents. A search retrieves 25 documents, of which 20 are relevant. What are the precision and recall?
questions.explanation: Precision = 20 ÷ 25 = 80% (relevant retrieved ÷ total retrieved); recall = 20 ÷ 50 = 40% (relevant retrieved ÷ total relevant).

questions.stem: A database contains 500 documents, 100 of which are relevant. A search retrieves 50 documents, of which 35 are relevant. What are the precision, recall, and fallout?
questions.explanation: Precision = 35 ÷ 50 = 70%; recall = 35 ÷ 100 = 35%; non-relevant retrieved = 15, total non-relevant = 400, so fallout = 15 ÷ 400 = 3.75%.

questions.stem: What does it mean for a search to have high precision but low recall?

options.A: It retrieves almost every relevant document, along with many irrelevant ones
options.B: It returns no documents at all
options.D: Most of the documents it retrieves are relevant, but it misses a large share of the relevant documents that exist

questions.explanation: High precision means a large proportion of retrieved documents are relevant; low recall means many relevant documents were not retrieved — typically a narrow search strategy.
Fallout measures the proportion of non-relevant documents retrieved out of all non-relevant documents: FP ÷ (FP + TN). The other formulas give precision and recall.

questions.stem: Which outcome category describes a document that is relevant but was not retrieved?
questions.explanation: A false negative is a relevant document that was not retrieved; a false positive is a non-relevant document that was retrieved anyway.
